item.description: The September 3 Wake Up with the Metro Chamber event will focus on homelessness as one of the region's most significant economic, public safety, humanitarian, and quality-of-life challenges. The goal is to create a practical, data-driven discussion around outcomes, accountability, and effective solutions. We’ll gain a better understanding of where resources are currently invested and what results those investments are producing, learn from successful models from other communities and regions, and explore what changes could produce better outcomes for individuals experiencing homelessness, taxpayers, businesses, and the broader community. 8:15–9:00 Coffee, Breakfast & Networking 9:00–10:30 Program featuring Nolan Sullivan, Health Services Agency Director, County of Sonoma and Sarah Fields, Deputy Director, Public Affairs | Housing Department, City of San José Tickets $45 member | $55 non-member by August 26 $55 member | $65 non-member after August 26 Table of 8 $375 member | $450 non-me

item.title: Mere Seconds + Insight/Incite 20/20 Photography Exhibition — Thu Sep 3, 4:00 PM — Sonoma State University Art Gallery
item.description:
The University Art Gallery at Sonoma State University is pleased to present two concurrent photography exhibitions: ***Mere Seconds: Andrew Owen*** and ***Insight/Incite 20/20: PhotoAlliance 20th Anniversary Portfolio.*** On view from **September 3 through October 17, 2026**, the exhibitions are guest-curated by Bay Area artist and Bass & Reiner Gallery co-founder Chris Grunder. item.description:
You Are Invited to Mare Island Toastmasters Meeting Each week, we have a different meeting theme. This week's theme is Impromptu Speaking
You are invited to a Toastmasters Meeting Date:
----Thursdays at Time: 7:30pm Pacific Time Place-: --online weekly, but in-person only on the 1st and 2nd Thursdays
From workplace conversations to social situations and community roles, the ability to speak clearly and confidently without preparation is one of the most practical communication skills you can develop. At Toastmasters, impromptu speaking, what we call Table Topics, is practiced at each meeting. Yes, it can be daunting, even for the most experienced Toastmaster, but it is a trainable skill that we actually use every day.
Let’s look at what impromptu speaking really is, why it is so important, and how it applies directly to everyday life, not only the Toastmasters meeting room.

Sponsor: Marin Center
Link: http://www.marincounty.org/depts/cu
The Frank Lloyd Wright-designed Marin County Civic Center is a national- and state-designated historic landmark. Ninety minute docent-led tours of the Civic Center are offered every Wednesday and Friday at 10:30 am, leaving from the second floor Café, Room 233. item.title: Summer Movie Nights in the Grove at Raymond — Fri Sep 4, 6:00 PM — Raymond Vineyards
item.description:
Enjoy an evening under the stars at Raymond Vineyards with an outdoor screening of The Devil Wears Prada 2. Part of the Summer Movie Nights in the Grove series, this fun and nostalgic experience pairs a highly anticipated sequel with wine, light bites, and a beautiful vineyard setting. Guests can purchase wine by the glass or bottle and enjoy additional bites throughout the evening while watching the movie beneath the night sky. item.title: Sourdough Bread Basics — Sat Sep 5, 10:30 AM — Gather Sebastopol
item.description:
Dive into the world of sourdough baking in this hands-on class! Learn how to create and feed a sourdough starter, master the basics of bulk fermentation, and shape different types of loaves. Along the way, you’ll gain an understanding of timing, technique, and the simple ingredients that make sourdough bread so special.
Perfect for beginners ready to explore artisan breadmaking, this workshop gives you both the knowledge and practice to confidently bake at home.
You’ll take home:
• A lively sourdough starter to keep your baking journey going.
• One pre-bulk fermented loaf, shaped in class, ready to bake the same day.
• One freshly mixed boule to ferment overnight and bake the next day.

item.title: Arjun Verma - Northern Classical Indian Concert — Sat Sep 5, 2:00 PM — Windsor Regional Library
item.description:
Immerse yourself in Northern Indian Classical music featuring sitar and tabla. Arjun K. Verma is an Indian-American sitarist and composer. Beginning with his father, Roop Verma, and continuing with the legendary Ali Akbar Khan and his son Alam Khan, Arjun's meticulous training has imbued him with a rich musicality that encompasses both the profound majesty and the exhilaration of North Indian classical music. Hailed by the New York Times as a "fine sitarist," Arjun shares the jewels of his cultural heritage in a manner that is fresh, modern, and relevant, while maintaining a high standard of traditional integrity.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.description:
Building on the skills and confidence you developed in the first class, this watercolor workshop invites you to take your ideas a step further. Explore how a simple sketch, thoughtful composition, and expressive use of color can transform an idea into a finished painting.
We'll work larger and bolder while exploring watercolor techniques including:
Wet-on-wet paintingLoose interpretation and expressive mark-makingCreating shadows and depthEnhancing backgroundsWorking in black and whiteExploring the many variations and possibilities of mixing greens
Bring a favorite photograph, a live flower or small plant, or even a meaningful memory to use as inspiration. No matter where you are in your artistic journey, you'll be encouraged to experiment, have fun, and focus on the larger picture rather than striving for perfection. There are no mistakes in art—only opportunities to explore.
Please Note: There will be a $10 supply fee paid directly to the Nancy on the day of the class.
